_: THE ASSET TABLE — every image, video and audio file in both repos. Scanned fields are rewritten by `node tools/asset-table.mjs --scan`; the six judged fields (what · quality · qualityNote · verdict · revealArc · bucket) are hand-written and a scan never touches them.
_purpose: Nothing ships without Mike's personal inspection — and Mike must not have to perfect assets in advance. Slots move, things change, some of these are never needed. This table exists so an inspection can be generated on demand for whatever is actually about to ship, instead of demanding a verdict on everything up front.
_quality: Ops' honest read of the FILE, never of the idea: usable | weak | wrong | placeholder | null. `null` means NOBODY HAS LOOKED, and it is not a passing grade. `wrong` means the file does not show what its slot says it shows.
_verdict: MIKE'S, and unset by default. null = not inspected. Values are his to choose; `pass` and `reject` are what the checklist reads. Ops never writes this field.
_bucket: THE BOUNCY BALL BUCKET (Mike, 2026-08-07): precious | dump | null. The law caps POINTS OF FOCUS, not assets — humans remember one or two things, and ten things reduces the odds they keep the one that matters. PRECIOUS is a genuine reveal, two or three A WEEK, and those are what a reader remembers. DUMP is everything else: fun to look at, part of the story, part of the pile, and there is NO CEILING on it — ten manual pages arriving is one point of focus, not ten. `null` means UNASSIGNED and is not a third bucket. Ops never writes this field, and deliberately does not derive it: a heuristic here would make the runway report look answered when nothing had been answered. The law and the two runways live in `reveal/focus.mjs`.
_gate: THE RECORD APPROVAL GATE (Mike, 2026-08-04): final sign-off on a Record is Mike personally inspecting EVERY thing presented in it. `--checklist` is how that inspection is produced; a Record with any presented asset at verdict null has not been signed off.

entries.what: The MGK-NIAC album cover — the house ROBOTS template with the machine's own head, lens forward, set into the disc the WB mark used to occupy, and the model number where the word ROBOTS was.
entries.qualityNote: THE FURNITURE IS EXACT AND THE BADGE IS THE WHOLE CABINET. Every constant is lifted from tools/make_robots_cover.py, so the ground, the border, the setting, the rule and the strapline are the front desk's own to the pixel. [K1 2026-08-07] THIS NOTE WAS THREE ROUNDS STALE AND NAMED A FILE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS — it described the head_lens.jpg badge and the argument that the museum held no photograph of this machine whole. Both were overtaken: R4 swapped the badge to core_helical.jpg, P7 swapped it again to cabinet_whole.jpg, which IS the first photograph of the mainframe whole, and D5 made it ride the ring as a plate rather than a cut-out because the frame is cropped at the cabinet's own bounding box and has no room in it to matte away. head_lens.jpg was deleted with the other ten operator plates at K1. The badge is 858x1438 fitted whole into the disc's inscribed box (focal = None), so the paper shows in the disc's corners by design and nothing of the machine is cropped away. Register P4 — a frame with air around the object, which is what a true cut-out would need — is still open and is a photograph Mike brings.

entries.what: The MGK-VIIIp album cover — the house ROBOTS template with the whole unit in the disc and the model number below it.
entries.qualityNote: This is the instruction met exactly: front_full.png is the unit, square on, whole, sharp, and the disc crop takes it without cutting the machine. The faceplate and the lit glass are legible inside the badge at full size, which is a bonus rather than the point — at deck size it reads as an object. Two departures from the base cover, both deliberate and both applied to BOTH machine covers so the pair cannot drift: the rule sits 14px lower so this name's descender clears it, and the letter-tracking is solved per cover so nine glyphs set inside the measure six do. The word still runs wider than the rule beneath it, which the six-glyph cover does not — the one place the pair is visibly unequal.

entries.what: MGK-NIAC plate 1 of 4, and the album cover's badge — the helical core through the cage bars.
entries.qualityNote: THE ONE UNMISTAKABLE FEATURE OF THE MAINFRAME, and the reason it is the cover: a blue coil down the middle of a cabinet, read through a grid of bars, with the element's warm flanks either side of it. 380x820, so it is a TALL frame and the cover's circular badge takes a square out of it — the crop rides high (focal 0.36) so the disc holds coil rather than the core's foot and the loose cable. Soft, as every frame lifted from 2021 phone video is; at badge size that reads as depth rather than as blur. FOR MIKE: the blue is the whole of what makes this frame, and the wing's B&W law takes it at the glass — the file keeps its colour on disk.

entries.what: MGK-NIAC plate 4 of 4, and the album's viewer poster — the interior flooded red-orange.
entries.qualityNote: THE MOST DRAMATIC FRAME IN THE SET and the one that most looks like a 1965 machine in trouble: the whole cage red, the element glowing through it, the core's helix still legible as a separate blue-white line. 560x740. FOR MIKE, AND IT IS A QUESTION RATHER THAN A DEFECT: the robots repo's own record of this frame calls it the meltdown and quotes you on tape saying so, but nothing in the MUSEUM's fiction says this machine has ever been in trouble. The caption states what the frame shows and stops there. If a fault is part of NIAC's story, this plate is where it starts.

entries.what: MGK-NIAC plate 3 of 4, and the still on TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS — the bar bank at the cabinet's base.
entries.qualityNote: THE OUTPUT ROW, MID-PATTERN, which is the only frame in either repository showing this machine SAYING something. Two banks of red bar-graph modules behind the bars with a dark square aperture between them; the lit segments are uneven across the banks, which is what makes it read as a readout rather than as a lamp test. 690x240 — a wide letterbox, so it will sit in a collage tile with generous mat above and below and it is the wrong shape for any square slot. It carries the TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS face's own 1 x 64 entry as a picture.

_revealArc: THE REVEAL ARC (Mike, 2026-08-04): arrived | understood | partial | online | null. The house's canon for how a thing is revealed — acknowledged when it arrived, status-updated as it was understood, brought online in stages — applied to every asset so a visitor can be given the sequence the house actually lived, test patterns and noise included. `null` means UNSET and is not a stage: it is the honest state of an asset whose arc nobody has established. Ops populates only what the record already attests.
_uid: [C32 2026-08-05] THE ROW'S NAME, minted once and never rewritten. `id` is repo:path and is an ADDRESS — it changes when a file moves. `uid` does not, so a judgement hangs off something a rename cannot touch. Other tables may reference a row by uid; nothing may reference it by path and expect that to hold.
_sha256: [C32 2026-08-05] The content hash, re-measured every scan. A prior row and a new file sharing a hash inside one repo are the same file MOVED: the scan carries the judgement and the uid across and reports it. Where a rename ALSO changed the content — the ordinary case, because the name is usually in the picture — no hash can see it, so the judged row is surfaced under its own banner and `--rename` is the explicit declaration that moves it. The silence was the defect; the hash only makes it rarer.
